title: Tenant signals and proactive graceful-degradation playbook for dedicated clusters
creator: Anya Patel
description: After the capacity event on 2026-01-29 we observed repeated eviction cascades in several dedicated clusters caused by sudden tenant-level KV cache amplification and unexpected synchronous burst patterns. This ticket captures a playbook that: 1) defines a lightweight tenant 'signal' model used for early noisy-neighbor detection, 2) implements a graduated graceful-degradation (soft-throttle + model-variant fallback) path to keep critical traffic healthy, and 3) automates reservation correction suggestions when utilization patterns show sustained mis-sizing. The intent is to reduce blast radius of surges, shorten MTTI/MTTR for capacity events, and provide deterministic behavior for downstream platform teams. This is an engineering-facing operational project: design + infra + runtime changes and a short rollout plan with observability hooks.
acceptance_criteria: Tenant signal pipeline emits a 'noisy_score' per-tenant with <=60s latency and documented schema
Soft-degradation policy implemented in the admission layer that triggers at noisy_score >= 0.7 and gracefully reduces per-tenant concurrency or routes to a low-cost compatible model variant
Automated reservation audit job that produces recommended reservation delta for each tenant with historical utilization window configurable (default 24h)
End-to-end integration tests and a canary rollout on one dedicated pool demonstrating reduced eviction rate for injected synthetic noisy tenants
Dashboard panels for noisy_score, soft-degrade events, eviction rate, and reservation recommendation drift created and linked
